title: SYS-01 user and project member report
source_system: Project management SaaS admin settings (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: The owner's account is the only administrator; 23 external portal users (subcontractor staff and client representatives), each invited by the owner by email, listed with company name and last sign-in date; the FC-1 project lists 6 subcontractor companies as members; no record of a user list review

title: SYS-01 security, permission and export settings
source_system: Project management SaaS admin settings (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Administrator sign-in uses a password only; MFA by authenticator app is offered for the administrator and for all users and is turned off; the default subcontractor permission template gives view access to the whole project folder, including other subcontractors' pricing and the full drawing set; a user activity screen records sign-ins and changes on the vendor's platform; the export history lists no project data export

title: Project management vendor SOC 2 Type 2 report and bridge letter
source_system: Project management SaaS vendor (provided on request)
what_it_shows: Type 2 report on the Security and Availability categories for the 12 months ending 2026-03-31, unqualified opinion, no exceptions noted; bridge letter through 2026-06-30; the system description covers the web and mobile apps, document storage, the pay application module and the subcontractor portal, and states RTO 4 hours and RPO 1 hour, encryption at rest and TLS in transit, and backups that are encrypted, checked for integrity and kept in a separate location; the cloud hosting provider is a carved-out subservice organization; complementary user entity controls listed: enable MFA, provision and remove users, assign permission templates, review activity, keep own exports; the vendor commits to notify affected customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident; no FedRAMP authorization is claimed

title: Accounting SaaS user, security and vendor settings
source_system: Accounting SaaS admin settings (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: One user login, the owner's, with administrator rights; password sign-in only, with MFA offered and turned off; password last changed in 2023; the sign-in history shows sign-ins from a second computer during the bookkeeper's monthly sessions; vendor records hold subcontractor and supplier bank details; ACH bill pay and the bank feed are connected; alerts on vendor bank-detail changes are off; 1099 tracking holds W-9 files for the 8 subcontractors who are sole proprietors, with their Social Security numbers

title: Accounting SaaS receivables, payables and vendor reports, 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30
source_system: Accounting SaaS reporting (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: About $15,000 billed in a typical month, by pay apps with a schedule of values on larger jobs and invoices on small ones; about $9,000 paid out to subcontractors and suppliers in a typical month, by ACH from the bank portal or by check; about 14 trade subcontractors and 6 suppliers paid in 2026; private clients paid by ACH or check and the VA by EFT; no card payments received

title: 2025 Schedule C (Form 1040)
source_system: Owner's tax files (prepared by the CPA firm from the accounting SaaS export)
what_it_shows: Gross receipts of about $180,000; no wages paid; the business is a sole proprietorship operating under the owner's trade name; trade work paid to subcontractors as contract labor

title: Business email and file account security page and admin console
source_system: Business email and file storage admin console (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: Small business productivity plan with 1 licensed user on the company domain; 2-step verification by text message code, turned on in 2024; the provider keeps a sign-in history and a record of mailbox forwarding and inbox rules, with no record of a review; the provider scans attachments; file storage offers version history, and the laptop work folder is not synced to it

title: Company domain DNS records
source_system: Domain registrar account
what_it_shows: The domain publishes an SPF record; no DKIM or DMARC record is published; no domain monitoring or look-alike domain alert service is on the account

title: Inbox review of payment and project correspondence, 2025-07-01 to 2026-07-08
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: Pay apps, lien waivers, subcontractor invoices and quotes, and payment correspondence are sent and received by email; earlier bank-detail changes from subcontractors were requested by email and confirmed by email reply, with no record of a call-back; W-9 forms with Social Security numbers sit as attachments in the mailbox; subcontractors send drawings and submittals through free file-transfer links

title: March 2026 bank-change email and phone call log
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-03); phone call log (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: An email appearing to come from the electrical subcontractor asked the owner to change its bank account before the next payment; the phone's call log shows a call that day from the subcontractor's number in the signed subcontract; the owner's note on the thread records that the subcontractor, calling about another matter, said it had not changed its account; the accounting vendor record was not changed

title: Standard subcontract, client contract and pay app cover sheet forms, with the signed 2026 subcontracts
source_system: Signed agreements file cabinet (home office); file storage (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: Every 2026 job has written subcontracts on the owner's standard form; the form says the subcontractor follows all applicable federal clauses and does not set out the text or substance of FAR 52.204-21 or 52.204-25, and has no security, confidentiality or incident notice terms; the 6 FC-1 subcontracts use this form; the client contract form and the pay app cover sheet say nothing about how the company will or will not change its remittance details

title: FC-1 contract award
source_system: Contract file (SYS-03 file storage)
what_it_shows: Firm-fixed-price contract with the Department of Veterans Affairs to renovate a staff break room and two offices at a community-based outpatient clinic in Florida, about $68,000, awarded 2026-03-09 under a small business set-aside, performance through 2026-11; includes FAR 52.204-21, 52.204-23, 52.204-25, 52.222-8, 52.232-27 and 52.232-33; construction wage rate requirements apply, with weekly certified payrolls; payment by EFT to the bank account in SAM

title: Prime contractor's request for proposal for the DoD subcontract
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: Interior renovation work of about $45,000 under the prime's DoD task order at an Army Reserve Center in Florida, award expected 2026-12; the task order includes DFARS 252.204-7021 at CMMC Level 1 (Self); the prime requires a current Final Level 1 (Self) status with an affirmation in SPRS before the subcontract is awarded; no CUI is expected; the scope includes a wireless door-access upgrade

title: SAM entity registration and government sign-in account
source_system: SAM.gov and the government sign-in service (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: Active registration under the trade name with a CAGE code and EFT bank information; the owner is the only Entity Administrator; representations and certifications renewed in January 2026, answering 'does not use' to the FAR 52.204-26 covered telecommunications representation; the government sign-in service requires the authenticator app on the owner's phone; the sign-in account is used for SAM and the federal invoicing portal; no SPRS account exists

title: Online banking user, payee and ACH settings
source_system: Business online banking (SYS-07)
what_it_shows: One user, the owner, who is also the only signer; the bank requires approval in the bank app for each new payee and each ACH batch; daily ACH limit of $30,000; ACH, wires and mobile deposit available; positive pay is not set up

title: Bank and card statements, 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30
source_system: Business bank account and card statements
what_it_shows: Recurring payments to the project management SaaS vendor, the accounting SaaS vendor, the email and file plan, the domain registrar, the website builder, the phone carrier, the internet provider, the self-storage facility and the general liability and tool insurer; the AI bid assistant subscription from 2026-03; hourly payments to the IT technician; monthly payments to the bookkeeper; an annual fee to the CPA firm; a laptop purchase in 2026-02; no payment for a cyber insurance policy

title: Phone carrier account and order history
source_system: Phone carrier account portal
what_it_shows: The owner's phone line and a carrier-branded mobile hotspot line with its device are on the account, with monthly data use on the hotspot; the previous phone was traded in at a carrier store in 2025, and no wipe confirmation is kept

title: Laptop settings and contents review
source_system: Laptop settings screens (SYS-04)
what_it_shows: One login with administrator rights, used by the owner and by family members; full-disk encryption on since purchase in 2026-02, with the recovery key saved in the owner's account and on paper in the home office safe; built-in antivirus on with real-time scanning, a weekly scheduled scan and automatic definition updates; automatic operating system updates on and current; host firewall on; no backup configured; the work folder holds estimates, scanned lien waivers and W-9 forms that are not copied anywhere else; passwords are saved in the browser

title: Phone settings and content review
source_system: Phone settings screens (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: Passcode and biometric unlock; device encryption on; automatic updates on; installs come from the official app store only; the phone receives the email text-message codes and holds the bank app and the authenticator app for the government sign-in service, with no other second factor registered on those accounts; find-and-wipe is not turned on; the camera roll, including FC-1 jobsite photos, syncs to the owner's personal consumer cloud photo account

title: Home router app and internet gateway status
source_system: Router phone app; internet provider gateway status page (SYS-06)
what_it_shows: An owner-bought Wi-Fi router sits behind the internet provider's gateway and runs one network; the connected-device list shows the laptop, the owner's phone, family phones, a game console, a smart TV and a doorbell camera; the router firmware version dates from 2021 and the update history shows no update since setup

title: AI bid assistant account settings and project history
source_system: AI bid assistant account (SYS-09)
what_it_shows: Individual subscription opened in 2026-03; the 'use my content to improve the service' setting is on (the default); the project history lists about 20 bids and change orders, with uploaded private client drawings and specifications and FC-1 change-order drawings uploaded in 2026-06; outputs are quantity takeoffs, unit price suggestions and proposal letter drafts

title: AI bid assistant terms of service (individual plan)
source_system: AI bid assistant vendor website
what_it_shows: Click-through individual plan terms let the vendor use uploaded content to improve its service while the setting is on; the vendor's business plan offers terms that bar training on customer data, deletion on request, and MFA

title: Company social media page post history
source_system: Company social media page
what_it_shows: Only the owner's account posts to the page; an April 2026 jobsite photo shows an FC-1 floor plan taped to a wall; a screenshot of the post was saved

title: Website builder account and site settings
source_system: Website builder SaaS account
what_it_shows: The company website is hosted by the website builder, with the owner as the only editor; the pages hold the company description and contact details; no integration with the company's email, project management or accounting accounts is set up

title: General liability and tool policy declarations
source_system: Insurance agent portal
what_it_shows: General liability and tool coverage in force for 2026; the declarations list no cyber, funds transfer fraud or social engineering coverage; the owner asked the agent on 2026-07-09 whether any policy covers cyber or social engineering losses

title: Bookkeeper engagement letter and invoices
source_system: Signed agreements file cabinet; email inbox (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: Independent contractor engagement for bank and accounting reconciliation and 1099 preparation, invoiced at about 6 hours a month; the letter has no security, confidentiality or breach notice terms and does not say how the bookkeeper signs in; the previous bookkeeper's engagement ended in 2024

title: IT technician invoices
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: Hourly invoices for on-site help, including setup of the home router and of the laptop bought in 2026-02; no remote support plan or standing access is billed

title: 2026 job list and private client contracts
source_system: Accounting SaaS job list (SYS-02); signed agreements file cabinet
what_it_shows: 2 to 4 jobs active at a time; private jobs include a dental office tenant build-out (about $52,000), a church fellowship hall renovation (about $35,000) and small retail repairs; FC-1 is about 35% of expected 2026 receipts; the dental build-out contract and drawings cover construction work only, and no patient information is exchanged; most client contracts make the client's drawings confidential

title: Search of the owner's files for security documents
source_system: Laptop; file storage and email (SYS-03); home office file cabinet
what_it_shows: Not found: a written security policy, an FCI scope, an asset or device inventory, a system security plan, a risk assessment, a CMMC self-assessment, a record of a Section 889 inquiry, an incident plan or contact list, a device wipe or disposal record, a security training certificate, stored recovery codes, a retention rule for security records, or a standby arrangement with another contractor

title: Calendar entries for community shredding events
source_system: Owner's calendar (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: Old plan sets and bid documents taken to a community shredding event twice a year, in spring and fall; the events give no destruction record

title: Insurance agent's reply on cyber and social engineering coverage
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: The agent confirmed that the company has no cyber insurance and no funds transfer fraud or social engineering coverage, and that no cyber product has been placed

title: BIA self-review worksheet
source_system: Owner's written BIA worksheet, reviewed with the IT technician
what_it_shows: For each of the five business functions, the owner's account of the systems, vendors and people used, the manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss the function can tolerate; bid due times are fixed; FC-1 subcontractors must be paid within 7 days of the Government's payment and certified payrolls are due weekly; the owner is the only person who performs or authorizes each function

title: Risk walk-through of accounts, devices and the home network
source_system: Walk-through with the IT technician
what_it_shows: Where money and FCI move day to day (pay apps and bank-detail requests by email, the bank app on the phone, the SAM EFT details, the AI bid assistant, the personal photo cloud, file-transfer links); family use of the laptop and home network; the March 2026 bank-change email; the owner as the only person who can bill, pay or reach the federal portals; paper files in the home office and tools in the storage unit during hurricane season

title: Self-review against FAR 52.204-21, CMMC Level 1 and Section 889
source_system: Owner's written answers to the requirement questions, checked on screen with the IT technician
what_it_shows: Passwords are owner-chosen with some reuse and no password manager, and the SAM password was used elsewhere before 2026; nobody reviews email sign-ins, forwarding rules or SYS-01 activity; non-household visitors to the home office (a client, the IT technician) are rare and always with the owner, with no written rule; a spare storage-unit padlock key lent to a subcontractor in 2025 was not returned, and jobsite lockbox codes are reused across jobs; incoming documents are not checked for CUI markings; no process exists for lower-tier subcontractors' CMMC status, and most trade subcontractors are one- to five-person firms; the owner has no SPRS access; no retention rule for security records

title: SYS-01 user list export checked against job closeouts
source_system: Project management SaaS admin settings (SYS-01); 2026 job list
what_it_shows: Of the 23 external portal users, 9 belong to subcontractors and client representatives from jobs closed in 2025 and were still active; each of the 6 FC-1 subcontractor companies has users on the default subcontractor template

title: Contract file review for CUI
source_system: FC-1 contract file; prime contractor's request for proposal
what_it_shows: No CUI markings on the FC-1 documents or in the prime's request; FC-1 is a VA civilian contract; the prime's request states that no CUI is expected

title: Walk-through of the home office, truck and storage unit, with device and key count
source_system: Home office, truck and self-storage unit (observation)
what_it_shows: The home office door has no lock, and family and guests pass through the room; signed subcontracts, lien waivers and certified payroll copies are in the home office file cabinet; current plan sets ride in the truck cab in plain view; the storage unit has a facility gate code and the owner's padlock, and the facility keeps its own gate log; no record is kept of who enters the home office or storage unit; keys and codes counted: office (no lock), storage padlock, truck; the laptop replaced in 2026-02 sits in a drawer, not wiped; the doorbell camera is household equipment not used for company work

title: Mailbox and file review for FCI
source_system: Email inbox and file storage (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: Free file-transfer links from subcontractors in the mailbox include FC-1 drawings and submittals, held on services outside the company's accounts

title: Section 889 inquiry notes and device labels
source_system: Device labels and purchase records; the producers named in FAR 52.204-25(a)
what_it_shows: The carrier-branded mobile hotspot used to connect the laptop at jobsites, including FC-1, is labeled as produced by a telecommunications manufacturer named in FAR 52.204-25(a); the laptop, the replaced laptop, the phone, the router and the internet provider's gateway are not from a named producer; the owner stopped using the hotspot that day and switched to phone tethering

title: FC-1 submittal log review
source_system: FC-1 submittal log (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: FC-1 submittals cover exhaust fans, lighting, door hardware and finishes, with no telecommunications, camera or network equipment; no submittal screening step existed before this review

title: Section 889 report to the FC-1 Contracting Officer
source_system: Sent email and Contracting Officer reply (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: Report of the covered hotspot sent to the FC-1 Contracting Officer on 2026-07-17, one business day after the 2026-07-16 discovery; the Contracting Officer acknowledged receipt; no written reporting procedure existed before this report

title: Section 889 10-business-day follow-up report
source_system: Sent email (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: Follow-up report sent to the FC-1 Contracting Officer on 2026-07-29, describing the mitigation: hotspot use stopped, phone tethering in use, and the device to be returned to the carrier

title: AI bid assistant back-test on 3 completed jobs
source_system: AI bid assistant account (SYS-09); the owner's final takeoffs and subcontractor quotes
what_it_shows: Takeoffs compared with the owner's final takeoffs on 3 completed jobs (dental build-out, church hall, one retail repair): drywall, paint and flooring areas within 4%; door, hardware and plumbing fixture counts 9% off on average, with items missed on revised sheets; demolition quantities 18% off; suggested unit prices 12% to 20% below local subcontractor quotes; two proposal letter drafts listed exclusions the owner had not chosen

title: Control assessment: External systems review
source_system: Phone photo settings; AI bid assistant upload history and terms; bookkeeper engagement letter; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The bookkeeper reaches SYS-02 from her own computer with no terms on how that device is protected; FC-1 drawings and photos were stored in the AI bid assistant and a personal consumer photo cloud with no terms the owner had checked; no external system types (personal cloud, free file-transfer links, consumer AI tools) were prohibited

title: Control assessment: Supply chain purchase check review
source_system: Section 889 inquiry notes 2026-07-16; device labels; purchase records; SAM representations; owner self-review
what_it_shows: No manufacturer check was made before buying devices, and the covered hotspot was bought without one; the 2026-07-16 inquiry checked every network and phone device label against the FAR 52.204-25(a) list and found the hotspot; hotspot use stopped the same day, phone tethering is used instead, and reports were filed on 2026-07-17 and 2026-07-29

title: Control assessment: MFA sign-in test (administrator accounts)
source_system: SYS-01, SYS-02 and SYS-03 security settings; sign-in tests from a new browser
what_it_shows: Email required a text-message code; the SYS-01 and SYS-02 administrator accounts signed in with a password only; both vendors offer app-based MFA at no cost

title: Control assessment: External user sign-in settings
source_system: SYS-01 user list and security settings
what_it_shows: The 23 external SYS-01 users (subcontractors and client representatives) sign in with a password only

title: Control assessment: Password and default credential test
source_system: Router administration page; password manager status; accounting user list; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The home router accepted the manufacturer's default administrator password, with remote administration on; the owner changed the password and turned remote administration off during the test; the owner creates every account, and portal invitations go only to email addresses in signed subcontracts as one-time vendor links; some owner passwords are reused across services; no procedure for a lost phone or compromised password and no stored recovery codes; the accounting password dates from 2023 and was not changed when the previous bookkeeper's engagement ended in 2024; passwords are saved in the browser on the laptop login family members also use; the bookkeeper knows the owner's accounting password; no written password rule at the time of testing; the laptop and phone keep credentials in encrypted system keychains, and the phone authenticator is protected by biometrics

title: Control assessment: Home network boundary test
source_system: Router settings and connected-device list; laptop firewall; external check of the router's remote administration port
what_it_shows: Nobody looks at router or gateway activity, and the router keeps no useful log; inbound traffic is blocked by the provider gateway and the laptop firewall, but the router's remote administration page answered from the internet until it was turned off on 2026-07-21; no monitoring between the laptop and other devices on the home network; family devices, a game console, a smart TV and a doorbell camera share one network with the laptop; no publicly accessible components inside the boundary; the laptop connected at jobsites through the covered mobile hotspot until 2026-07-16, and phone tethering is now used

title: Control assessment: Encryption status check
source_system: Laptop and phone encryption status screens; SYS-01 vendor SOC 2 report
what_it_shows: Laptop full-disk encryption on and verified; phone encrypted by its passcode; SYS-01 encrypted at rest by the vendor (SOC 2 report)

title: Control assessment: Malicious code protection test
source_system: Antivirus status page; standard antivirus test file downloaded on 2026-07-21
what_it_shows: The built-in antivirus detected the test file on download, quarantined and removed it, and showed an alert to the owner; definitions update automatically (last update the same day); weekly full scan scheduled (last run 2026-07-19); real-time protection on for downloads and attachments; the default action quarantines detections; the owner checks the quarantine list when alerted, and no false positives are recorded

title: Control assessment: Backup review
source_system: SYS-01 vendor SOC 2 report; laptop storage review; email file storage settings; owner self-review
what_it_shows: Estimates, scanned lien waivers and W-9 forms on the laptop have no backup; security documents (this assessment, P01 to P06) were only on the laptop until moved to the business file storage; the SYS-01 vendor backs up the platform, encrypts backups, checks their integrity and keeps them in a separate location (SOC 2 report, no exceptions in backup testing)

title: Control assessment: Incident reporting self-review
source_system: Contact lists; bookkeeper engagement letter; subcontract form; Section 889 report; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The bookkeeper, IT technician and subcontractors have no duty or time limit to tell the owner about suspicious payment requests or account problems; no list of whom to notify (bank fraud line, IC3, clients, Florida Department of Legal Affairs); the Section 889 report went to the Contracting Officer within 1 business day
